claims.quote: `["string/join", list, separator]` is a list of strings with the separator between them. With a third string, that one stands before the last item, as `#:before-last` does in Racket: `["string/join", ["array/make", "a", "b", "c"], ", ", " and "]` is `"a, b and c"`.

`number/toString` takes a second argument, a string to write between groups of three digits of the whole part, as `#:group-sep` does in Racket: `["number/toString", 1234567.5, ","]` is `"1,234,567.5"`. With one argument it is unchanged.

claims.quote: A record keeps the key `""`, as JSON does. `{"": 1, "a": 2}` used to evaluate to `{"a": 2}`, and so did the same record inside `quote`, in a fact, in a pattern, and in a snapshot; `["object/keys", ["quote", {"": 1}]]` was `[]`. Every record now keeps every key JSON allows except `__proto__`, so a pattern such as `{"": "?v"}` takes the value apart, and a snapshot writes it back. The graph editor's dialog still asks for a property name, and now says so instead of saying keys must be non-empty.
